direct_experimental_variant_effects.gap: Genomic placement is incomplete: 1,040 of 1,402 sets (74.2%) have at least one genomic-coordinate product (990 through Ensembl's codon expansion, 191 through MaveDB's own mapper, 141 through both) and 362 have neither. Ensembl expands each protein-level variant into every codon-compatible allele; MaveDB's mapper gives genomic HGVS to about 317k of 3.07M annotated variants. 197 of our sets are absent from the CC0 dump (62 non-CC0, 134 published after the dump date, 1 unexplained: urn:mavedb:00001251-a-1). 51 superseded human-target sets exist only as a labelled extension. Scores are not comparable across sets and calibrations exist for few sets.
direct_experimental_variant_effects.next: Build one variant-level table keyed by VRS digest or ClinGen allele ID that links assay variant, mapped alleles and annotations; treat superseded versions explicitly; do not pool raw scores across sets.

protein_structure_function.gap: UniProt reviewed entries, the humsavar variant index, AlphaFold DB canonical models with per-residue confidence and InterPro/member-database matches are acquired for the 549 UniProt accessions of the MaveDB set. Seven very long proteins have only isoform models in AlphaFold DB (recorded, not stored as canonical) and 13 accessions have no model. Variant-level stability and structural-effect predictors (Ensembl ProtVar 1.3 GB, mutfunc 2.0 GB) are not fetched; FoldX and AlphaMissense values reach us only through the Open Targets variant index and AlphaMissense tables. Experimental structures (PDB) are not catalogued.
protein_structure_function.next: Map MaveDB residue positions onto AlphaFold coordinates and InterPro domains for position-level features; evaluate ProtVar and mutfunc for variant-level structural effects.

regulation_expression_splicing.gap: Acquired: GTEx median expression, SCREEN cCRE intervals, Open Targets enhancer-to-gene links (48.8M intervals) and the molecular-QTL part of the Open Targets study and credible-set tables (eQTL, sQTL, tuQTL, pQTL, single-cell eQTL). Not acquired: raw eQTL summary statistics (eQTL Catalogue FTP is large; its licence is CC BY 4.0), genome-wide splicing predictors (SpliceAI 27 GB, SpliceVault 843 MB; SpliceAI and Pangolin scores are available per variant in the gnomAD slices) and sequence-to-function predictions (Enformer 2.8 GB). cCREs and enhancer links are predictions, not variant effects.
regulation_expression_splicing.next: Use the gnomAD slice scores for variants of interest; evaluate SpliceVault; use the MPRA score sets already in MaveDB for regulatory variants; fetch eQTL Catalogue credible sets only for loci that need them.

perturbation_evidence.gap: Acquired and joined to MaveDB genes: BioGRID ORCS human screens (MIT licence), Open Targets target_essentiality (DepMap-derived), CRISPR-screen evidence and IMPC mouse knockout evidence. DepMap's own portal is behind a human-verification wall and was not fetched. No variant-level perturbation (base-editing) source is catalogued.
perturbation_evidence.next: User downloads DepMap Public manually if the original files are needed; assess base-editor screen repositories.

natural_knockouts_dosage.gap: gnomAD v4.1.2 constraint, ClinGen haploinsufficiency/triplosensitivity gene and region sets, and Open Targets gene-burden evidence are acquired. Not covered: gnomAD LoF curation and homozygous-LoF counts.
natural_knockouts_dosage.next: Fetch gnomAD lof_curation (listed on the downloads page, contents not opened).

association_finemapping_coloc.gap: Acquired: the flat GWAS Catalog associations table and, from Open Targets, 3.0M studies, 4.76M credible sets (GWAS and molecular QTL), 3.29M locus-to-gene predictions and the 7.89M-variant index. Not acquired: colocalisation (15.4 GiB), LD and haplotype reference panels (the 1000 Genomes phased panel can be sliced by remote tabix like the gnomAD files), and eQTL Catalogue summary statistics.
association_finemapping_coloc.next: Decide the LD source and slice it by region; fetch colocalisation only for loci of interest (Open Targets GraphQL can serve single loci).

functional_haplotypes_pgx.gap: ClinPGx, CPIC and Open Targets pharmacogenomics tables are acquired. PharmVar's licence and bulk route are unverified, so star-allele sequence definitions are missing.
functional_haplotypes_pgx.next: Read PharmVar terms manually; use its API if permitted.

structural_variation_cnv.gap: Acquired: gnomAD v4.1 genome SV (2.15M records), gnomAD exome CNV, DGV GRCh38 (1.99M records, control cohorts) and ClinGen recurrent CNV and dosage regions. Not acquired: long-read SV callsets (gnomAD release/lr, 1000 Genomes/HGSVC). dbVar currency is unknown and DECIPHER denied access.
structural_variation_cnv.next: Inspect dbVar contents and dates; assess long-read SV catalogues.

repeat_expansions_str.gap: STRchive disease loci (82, hg38) are acquired. Population allele-size distributions (gnomAD TR) and genome-wide reference catalogues (PlatinumTRs, 7.8M loci) are not.
repeat_expansions_str.next: Fetch gnomAD tandem-repeat and PlatinumTRs data when STR calling is in scope.

pathways_interactions_epistasis.gap: Reactome mappings and the Open Targets aggregation of molecular interactions (IntAct, SIGNOR, Reactome, STRING: 14.6M interactions with 27.4M evidence records) are acquired. The interaction resources are held only in aggregated form. Nothing in the library quantifies epistasis or compensation, and digenic or oligogenic disease databases have not been assessed.
pathways_interactions_epistasis.next: Assess digenic and oligogenic resources; fetch IntAct or STRING directly only if the aggregation proves insufficient.

clinical_interpretation.gap: Acquired: ClinVar (2026-10-19), ClinGen gene-disease validity, UniProt humsavar (85,015 curated missense rows), and from Open Targets the disease ontology, HPO terms and phenotype links and gene-disease evidence from Genomics England PanelApp, Gene2Phenotype, Orphanet and UniProt. OMIM is licensed, Monarch/MONDO beyond the Open Targets ontology are not assessed, and DECIPHER is access-controlled.
clinical_interpretation.next: Assess Monarch and the HPO annotation files directly; keep ClinVar and humsavar release dates in every result.

population_frequency.gap: gnomAD v4.1 allele frequencies are held for the genomic positions of MaveDB-mapped SNVs only, as remote-tabix slices of the joint callset (exomes and genomes pooled: the frequency Open Targets and the MaveDB dump quote) and of the exome and genome callsets separately. Whole-chromosome VCFs (11-67 GiB each) are deliberately not mirrored, and an allele missing from a slice is not a frequency of zero. 1000 Genomes contributes a 3,202-sample population table only; phased panels for haplotype structure are not fetched.
population_frequency.next: Reuse the slicing script for any new variant or region set (use the joint slice as the frequency of record); slice the 1000 Genomes phased panel where LD is needed.

annotation_integration.gap: Acquired: AlphaMissense gene-level and full variant tables (71.7M rows), the in-silico scores carried in the gnomAD slices (CADD, REVEL, SpliceAI, Pangolin, PhyloP, SIFT, PolyPhen) and the variant-effect assessments in the Open Targets variant index (VEP, GERP, SIFT, FoldX, AlphaMissense, LOFTEE). dbNSFP, the broadest integrator, remains gated by institutional registration; Ensembl VEP caches and most plugin data are not fetched (only the MaveDB plugin file).
annotation_integration.next: Ask the user to register for dbNSFP; fetch the VEP GRCh38 cache and the SpliceAI/SpliceVault plugin data when whole-genome annotation begins.

reference_annotation.gap: MANE v1.5 summary and GTF, and the Open Targets target annotation (78,733 genes), GO, Sequence Ontology, homology and biosample tables are acquired; the Ensembl genome registry asset names the GRCh38.p14 reference. GENCODE v50 annotation and the genome FASTA are not fetched.
reference_annotation.next: Fetch GENCODE and the FASTA when sequence extraction is needed.

resource_catalogues.gap: OpenEBench tool counts are derived (the bio.tools API is bot-protected). FAIRsharing records are not harvested (its API needs an account).
resource_catalogues.next: Optional: the user supplies a FAIRsharing token.

background_documentation.gap: Background pages only (NHGRI glossary and 1000 Genomes project page); they carry no variant-level evidence.

needs.dbnsfp: User registers with an institutional email at dbnsfp.org and requests download links (about 50 GB); licence CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 forbids redistributing derivatives.
needs.depmap: User downloads DepMap Public files manually from the DepMap downloads page (the portal asks automated clients not to scrape), or use the Open Targets target_essentiality dataset already held.
needs.decipher: User applies for DECIPHER data access.
needs.pharmvar: Read the PharmVar terms of use manually, then use its API or downloads.
needs.fairsharing: User creates a FAIRsharing account or token if programmatic harvesting is wanted.
needs.eqtl_catalogue: Licence is CC BY 4.0 (verified). Summary statistics are on the FTP and are large; the REST API v2 is retired and v3 should be checked before use; metadata tables are hosted in a GitHub repository outside this session's scope.
needs.dbvar: Inspect FTP contents and dates before use.
needs.biotools: The bio.tools API is behind a bot challenge; OpenEBench is used instead.

not_yet_assessed: HPO annotation files and the Monarch Initiative / MONDO (the Open Targets copies of the ontologies are held, the originals are not assessed)
gnomAD tandem repeats, LoF curation and local-ancestry datasets (listed on the downloads page, contents not opened)
Haplotype and LD reference panels (HGDP+1kGP, 1000 Genomes high-coverage phased genotypes)
Interaction resources in their original form (IntAct, STRING, BioGRID interactions): only the Open Targets aggregation is held
Epistasis, digenic and oligogenic disease databases
Protein stability databases and benchmarks (ThermoMutDB, ProteinGym) and PTM databases
Standalone predictors outside dbNSFP and gnomAD INFO (SpliceAI as distributed by Illumina, ESM1b and popEVE scores)
ClinGen Allele Registry and ClinGen Variant Curation Expert Panel classifications beyond the files acquired
Regulatory variant-effect datasets outside MaveDB (MPRA/STARR-seq repositories)
Ensembl VEP plugin list and per-plugin licences (the documentation page returned HTTP 504 and then timed out)
